ops.title: yclaw is jj-colocated — detached git HEAD is steady-state; how to land multi-commit stacks non-interactively
ops.body:
The yclaw repo is jj-colocated (`.jj/` exists). Git's detached HEAD (`(HEAD detached from …)`, reflog "export from jj") is normal steady-state, NOT stranded work — jj exports its working-copy commit to git HEAD instead of moving a branch.

Landing a multi-commit stack non-interactively (verified 2026-07-07):
- `export JJ_EDITOR=true` first — `jj split -m` still opens an editor otherwise and hangs a non-interactive shell.
- `jj split <paths> -m 'msg'` peels those paths into a commit below `@`; repeat per concern, then `jj describe @ -m 'msg'` for the remainder.
- `jj bookmark set main -r <tip>` then `jj new main`; jj exports refs/heads/main to git immediately (verifiable with `git log main`).
- Rewriting an unlanded commit: `jj describe <rev> -m '…'` (e.g. to fix a commit trailer); `jj rebase -r <rev> -d <dest>` to stack it.
- The "jj config set --user user.name" hints are noise — authorship falls back to git config correctly.
- Gotcha: a git branch checked out in a `git worktree` (e.g. agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`) fights jj's ref export once jj rewrites that commit — remove the worktree (`git worktree remove --force`) and delete the branch after landing.
- In-guest hermes rebuilds read the repo share's COMMITTED main (see [[hermes-deploy-and-bluebubbles-addressing]]) — never move the main bookmark while a `just redeploy hermes` is mid-flight (dry-activate and switch would build different code).
